title: Self-Learning SuperTrend: An Adaptive Machine Learning-Based Trend Indicator

for: Backtesting results show Win Rate (Long/Short) improved from 48% / 46% (classic) to 61% / 59% (v2.00) on EURUSD H1, 2020–2025
Profit Factor increased from 0.91 (classic) to 1.42 (v2.00), a quantifiable, historically testable performance metric
Sharpe Ratio rose from 0.38 to 1.15 — directly computable from equity curve returns and volatility over the same 5-year backtest period
Maximum false signal streak reduced from 7 to 2 in a row over 5 years — a discrete, countable event verifiable in historical signal logs
Signal frequency dropped to ~1 per 18 bars (2.4 per 100 bars), enabling direct comparison of signal quality vs. quantity using historical entry/exit timestamps and outcomes
The background test matrix evaluates probe P&L and MAE over a fixed 5-bar horizon — a concrete, reproducible forward-looking window for validation
CalcProposals() generates parameter deltas based on rolling win rate, Sortino ratio, and consecutive losses — all derived from actual historical probe outcomes
Regime Grid uses DetectRegime() output (Hurst + Entropy + normalized ADX) and volatility — all computable from historical OHLC data without lookahead

Accuracy Layer v2.00 applies five explicit, timestamp-aligned filters (EMA crossover, ADX threshold ≥20, Keltner squeeze detection, candle body ratio, weighted confidence score) — each condition is binary/logical and replayable on past bars

L1 filtering updates feature weights via ApplyL1Shrinkage() using gradients computed from probe direction prediction error — error defined as sign(actual_return) − sign(predicted_direction), fully reconstructible from historical price moves

against: The trading signal depends on background virtual probes that evaluate forecast quality over a 5-bar horizon — this requires knowing price data 5 bars ahead at the time of signal generation (violates causality, future-data leakage). Specifically: 'After 5 bars, the probe is closed: the closing price is compared to the entry price...'. This means the indicator must wait 5 bars to assess probe outcomes before updating parameters or filtering signals — but the article presents the output (dots, buy/sell arrows, confidence) as real-time per-bar signals. The signal logic (e.g., final trend direction used for DotBullBuf/DotBearBuf) relies on adaptive parameters updated via CalcProposals(), which itself consumes probe results from a 5-bar look-ahead — thus the signal on bar i uses information from bars i+1 to i+5.

The Accuracy Layer v2.00 filters (e.g., EMA crossover, ADX threshold, Keltner squeeze) are defined and implemented, but the *exact condition for generating the primary trade signal* (i.e., the bullish/bearish trend flip that determines DotBullBuf/DotBearBuf placement) is never explicitly specified in formulaic terms. The text says: 'the second — the “signal” instance — uses adaptive parameters from the optimizer; its output determines the trend direction for signal generation', but no formula or pseudocode is given for how that 'signal instance' computes the trend direction — only that it's 'SuperTrend logic' with adaptive parameters. The core rule ('if price closes above/below adaptive band → trend change') is assumed but not written as a precise, self-contained condition using only past data — the adaptive bands themselves depend on the 5-bar lookahead via the optimizer.

The Hurst exponent calculation (in DetectRegime()) uses R/S analysis over a 64-bar window — standard R/S requires forward-looking range/standard deviation normalization or boundary-sensitive windowing; while the article states 'CalcHurst(close, idx, total, 64)', it gives no implementation details, and canonical R/S estimation on rolling windows often involves non-causal centering or look-ahead bias unless carefully implemented with strict series indexing — and the function signature 'close[], idx, total' suggests access to close[idx + i] for i up to 63 (see CheckKeltnerSqueeze usage pattern), meaning it reads up to 63 bars *ahead* of current bar idx (since idx is current, and it accesses close[idx + i] where i < len=64). This is confirmed by CheckKeltnerSqueeze: 'if(idx + len >= total) return(true); ... for(int i = 0; i < len; i++) emaVal += close[idx + i];' — same pattern applies to CalcHurst per its call signature and usage context.
non_fatal: No backtest outside sample is shown — but per instructions, this is non-fatal.
No mention of spread or commission modeling — non-fatal.
Uses MetaTrader-specific features (MQL5, iCustom, buffers) — but this is acceptable for spot forex as MT5 is standard retail platform; not fatal under criterion (3).
No martingale, grid, or averaging — criterion (4) not violated.
This is explicitly a trading indicator article, not infrastructure/graphic/optimizer-only — criterion (5) not violated.

judge.reject_reason: Фатальный порок: данные будущего в сигнале. Сигнал зависит от виртуальных проб, оцениваемых через 5 баров вперёд («After 5 bars, the probe is closed: the closing price is compared to the entry price»), а параметры адаптивного SuperTrend (которые определяют саму смену тренда — основное условие входа) обновляются функцией CalcProposals(), использующей результаты этих проб. Это приводит к утечке будущих данных: условие входа на баре i зависит от цен на барах i+1…i+5. Кроме того, функция DetectRegime() для расчёта режима рынка использует CalcHurst() с окном 64 бара, и контекст вызова (аналогично CheckKeltnerSqueeze) указывает на доступ к close[idx + i], т.е. к ценам вперёд — подтверждённая некорректная индексация с lookahead. Оба нарушения делают невозможным детерминированное воспроизведение правила на закрытых барах без будущих данных.
